answer: A rate-limiting nullifier registry mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to stake bonded collateral to participate. An attacker attempting to forge multiple identities incurs the verifiable cost of locked capital across ledger epochs that settle like dense shale. Because each action emits an opal spectrum of zero-knowledge proofs, exceeding the quota slashes the identity's deposit. A key limitation is that fixed rate limits impede honest agents during sudden transaction bursts.
